Flexible couple seeking a cheap short break

population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

rounds.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

decision.reason: The 480 member fare is a genuinely cheap escape after six months without leisure travel, and friends are flexible on dates and destination. Although this destination has little particular appeal, the low price and high trip interest make an optional break worthwhile; I would not pay the 600 normal fare if the member quota ran out.

person.segment_label: Flexible friends planning a cheap escape
person.eligibility_reason: This optional leisure departure fits the flexible travel window.
person.travel_party_context: Any companions can use this departure and independently arrange and fund their own tickets; this decision covers one existing member only.
person.booking_trigger: Friends have agreed to be flexible about dates and destination if a cheap escape appears; nobody is obliged to make the trip.
person.departure_time_tolerance: Can adapt to the displayed departure time for a worthwhile deal; no fixed appointment requires this flight.
person.value_context: The group enjoys bargain-led trips and can use this departure. This member chooses and pays only for their own ticket; a weak deal can still be declined.
person.outside_option: Suggest another leisure outing or save for a later trip; do not invent a quoted alternative fare.
person.motivation_context: Keen to arrange an optional break, with no ticket booked and no compulsory date or destination. Has not taken a leisure trip in the last six months. This destination is acceptable but has little particular attraction today. Skipping remains possible, though arranging a worthwhile leisure break is preferred.

analysis.summary: Sixteen members responded at a 480 HKD member fare. Four bought, all citing the member fare as a compelling bargain; two of these said they would decline at the 600 HKD normal fare. Nine declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and three were low-interest optional-trip declines where price was affordable but appeal was weak. The current fare sits at the permitted cap, so no higher test is allowed. Evidence is mixed: bargain-driven purchases coexist with availability and interest barriers.
analysis.hypothesis: At the same 480 HKD cap, removing inventory denials and testing fresh members will show whether conversion is limited by availability rather than fare; if denials persist, conversion stays near current levels regardless of price.

analysis.summary: At the current 312 HKD member fare, 7 of 16 customers bought and 9 declined. Among decliners, four cite unavailability/budget (environment forced), and five cite low interest, recent trips, or preference for free time rather than the fare itself. Buyers repeatedly call 312 a bargain versus 600. No customer objects to the price level; declines are driven by trip motivation, timing, or inventory. This suggests the fare is not the binding constraint, though the sample is small and optional-trip appeal is mixed.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce weighted conversion enough to lower basic ticket receipts, because current buyers describe 312 as a bargain and no decliner cites price as the main objection.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: Of 16 members, 5 bought at the 467 HKD fare and 11 declined. Eight declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), not price objections; three cited low interest or destination appeal, and one cited optional leisure. No customer objected to the fare itself, and buyers showed strong deal appeal. Evidence is mixed: the fare converts some price-sensitive members but most declines reflect unavailable inventory or weak trip motivation, so a directional price test is not clearly supported.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a lower fare on fresh members will not meaningfully raise conversion, because most declines stem from unavailable inventory or low trip interest rather than fare level; conversion should stay within a few points of the current rate.

analysis.summary: At the 332 HKD member fare, 8 of 16 customers bought and 8 declined. Most buyers cited the fare as a compelling bargain versus the 600 HKD normal fare, though several said they would not pay the normal fare. Declines were mainly low trip interest with a strong preference to keep money and schedule free, not price objections; three declines were inventory/budget-forced. No customer objected primarily to price, so the evidence does not clearly support lowering the fare further.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce weighted conversion enough to offset the higher per-ticket receipt, keeping basic receipts at or above the current level.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

Six declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), and four declines were low trip interest or destination appeal, not price objections. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at 333 does not prove willingness to pay more.

Three declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), and four were voluntary-trip objections citing low interest or low destination appeal, not price. Evidence points to testing a higher fare on fresh customers rather than lowering it.

analysis.summary: At the current 294 HKD member fare, 10 of 16 customers bought and 6 declined. Most buyers cited the low fare as a compelling bargain, often noting they would refuse the 600 HKD regular fare. Three declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and three were voluntary-trip refusals citing low destination interest or a recent trip, not price. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Evidence points to strong price sensitivity at the low end, but buying at 294 does not establish willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce member conversion enough to offset the higher per-ticket receipt, because current buyers cite the fare as a bargain well below their stated ceilings.

assumptions: Only existing members; no joining or renewal decision and no fee deduction.
Base fares only; all taxes/fuel/add-ons and operating costs excluded. Revenue is not airline profit.
Population weights are explicit scenario assumptions, not measured HK Express market shares.
Fresh stratified members each search round; paired candidate and initial quote in reset, blinded worlds. One seat per member per world.
Only declared public segment/flexibility enter learning; private budgets, motivation and simulator constraints remain environment-only.
Every third round may test a cited LLM direction within a bounded model-scored interval; text never adds a demand label.
Analyst requests allow at most three attempts within the shared call budget. Unavailable analysis supplies no direction; recorded purchases still train Thompson and undergo independent confirmation.
Quoted fares are whole HKD; weighted averages and statistical estimates may have decimals.
Parallel intent elicitation followed by fixed-priority integer inventory clearing; no seat is reserved by an LLM.
Weighted demand estimates and actual panel cash/seat transactions are reported separately.
Final member quotes round down to an amount ending in nine, with any result below HK$30 becoming HK$0; raw search prices remain recorded.
Independent validation compares the formatted initial fallback, formatted selected fare and no offer after freezing both final quotes; no refitting on holdout.
